analysis: Examined only test code. OnboardingChecks.swift head 1257-1262 adds expectations for ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild, which re-plans only once both Macs report the same new worker digest; missing or unanswered Macs wait. ClusterSupervisionChecks/main.swift head 248-330 adds checks for the coordinated pair update. The slot is keyed by pairing cluster ID. ClusterPairUpdate.partnerState waits until both Macs have staged the release and until both have drained. It gives up on partner failure, a different target release, or disabled auto-update. Stale progress, a silent partner, an unreachable partner, or an unknown phase yields cannotCoordinate or waiting, never ready. The request file (service-update-request.json) is taken once, and requests older than maximumAgeSeconds are dropped and removed. A progress-file round trip is also tested. These tests describe fail-safe availability behavior, aligned with A-018 (serving availability). No change to attestation, encryption, key custody, prefix cache (T-041) or authorization (TB-011) is visible here. No implementation source was supplied for ClusterPairUpdate, ClusterMemberUpdateSlot or ClusterOnboardingUpdate. Questions for integration: (1) where the request and progress files live, and whether they are owner-only (a same-UID process could forge partner progress or update requests, similar to the TB-012 local-process concerns); (2) how the partner's progress is transported between the Macs, and whether it is authenticated; (3) whether a forged 'gaveUp' state could indefinitely block updates, which would be a DoS on update freshness (T-043/T-047-like). Because these tests only exercise the logic, no regression is evidenced.
